knowledge:
- key_parameters: trimLeft=The number of nucleotides to remove from the start of each read ;; truncLen=The length at which to truncate forward and reverse reads ;; maxN=The maximum number of ambiguous nucleotides allowed (must be 0 for dada2) ;; maxEE=The maximum expected errors allowed in a read ;; compress=Whether to output filtered files as gzipped fastq files ;; multithread=Enables multithreading for faster computation
- alternatives: Traditional OTU-picking methods (e.g., QIIME's OTU picking) which cluster sequences at a threshold (usually 97%) rather than resolving exact amplicon sequence variants (ASVs).
- when_to_use: When analyzing high-throughput amplicon sequencing data (e.g., 16S rRNA, ITS, 18S) to resolve exact amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) with high sensitivity and specificity.
- pitfalls: Failing to remove non-biological bases (like PCR primers) before running the pipeline ;; Truncating reads too much (truncLen), which can reduce the overlap between forward and reverse reads to less than 20 nucleotides, preventing successful merging ;; Using inappropriate filtering/trimming parameters, as "one size does not fit all".

workflows.name: paired_end_denoising_pipeline
workflows.intent: Process raw paired-end FASTQ files to resolve exact amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) and construct a non-chimeric sequence table.
workflows.stages: 1. Inspect quality profiles using plotQualityProfile ;; 2. Filter and trim reads using filterAndTrim ;; 3. Dereplicate filtered reads using derepFastq ;; 4. Learn error rates using learnErrors ;; 5. Infer sample composition using dada ;; 6. Merge forward and reverse reads using mergePairs ;; 7. Construct sequence table using makeSequenceTable ;; 8. Remove chimeras using removeBimeraDenovo
workflows.code:
library(dada2); packageVersion("dada2")
fnF1 <- system.file("extdata", "sam1F.fastq.gz", package="dada2")
fnR1 <- system.file("extdata", "sam1R.fastq.gz", package="dada2")
filtF1 <- tempfile(fileext=".fastq.gz")
filtR1 <- tempfile(fileext=".fastq.gz")
plotQualityProfile(fnF1) # Forward
plotQualityProfile(fnR1) # Reverse
filterAndTrim(fwd=fnF1, filt=filtF1, rev=fnR1, filt.rev=filtR1,
                  trimLeft=10, truncLen=c(240, 200), 
                  maxN=0, maxEE=2,
                  compress=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
derepF1 <- derepFastq(filtF1, verbose=TRUE)
derepR1 <- derepFastq(filtR1, verbose=TRUE)
errF <- learnErrors(derepF1, multithread=FALSE) # multithreading is available on many functions
errR <- learnErrors(derepR1, multithread=FALSE)
dadaF1 <- dada(derepF1, err=errF, multithread=FALSE)
dadaR1 <- dada(derepR1, err=errR, multithread=FALSE)
print(dadaF1)
merger1 <- mergePairs(dadaF1, derepF1, dadaR1, derepR1, verbose=TRUE)
merger1.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(merger1, multithread=FALSE, verbose=TRUE)
fnF2 <- system.file("extdata", "sam2F.fastq.gz", package="dada2")
fnR2 <- system.file("extdata", "sam2R.fastq.gz", package="dada2")
filtF2 <- tempfile(fileext=".fastq.gz")
filtR2 <- tempfile(fileext=".fastq.gz")
filterAndTrim(fwd=fnF2, filt=filtF2, rev=fnR2, filt.rev=filtR2, maxN=0, trimLeft=10, truncLen=c(240, 200), maxEE=2, compress=TRUE, verbose=TRUE)
derepF2 <- derepFastq(filtF2, verbose=TRUE)
derepR2 <- derepFastq(filtR2, verbose=TRUE)
dadaF2 <- dada(derepF2, err=errF, multithread=FALSE)
dadaR2 <- dada(derepR2, err=errR, multithread=FALSE)
merger2 <- mergePairs(dadaF2, derepF2, dadaR2, derepR2, verbose=TRUE)
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(list(merger1, merger2))
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, verbose=TRUE)
dim(seqtab.nochim)
